summary.text: Tina Tartaglione is a Democratic state senator from Philadelphia who has represented Pennsylvania Senate District 2 since 1994 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026. She is the Senate Democratic Whip.

paragraphs.text: Christine M. Tartaglione was born September 21, 1960, in Philadelphia, and is a lifetime city resident, according to her official biography.
She attended St. Martin of Tours, St. Basil Academy, and Peirce Junior College.

She worked as an assistant to Philadelphia City Councilwoman Joan Krajewski from 1986 to 1989, as a senior executive assistant to State Treasurer Catherine Baker Knoll from 1989 to 1992, and as a business representative for United Food and Commercial Workers Local 1776 beginning in 1992.
In 1994 she became the fifth woman in state history to win election to the State Senate, and in 2010 she was elected Caucus Secretary, the first woman in Senate Democratic leadership.

She now serves as Senate Democratic Whip and as Democratic chair of the Intergovernmental Operations Committee, and she sits on the Labor and Industry; Law and Justice; Rules and Executive Nominations; and Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness committees.
Her biography says she authored Senate Bill 1090, Pennsylvania's 2006 minimum wage increase, and describes her as an advocate for working families and people with disabilities.
